panels.description: What running compactions have reserved against the node's ceiling. The peak is what says whether the ceiling is close to binding -- a scrape of the current value misses the bursts. A ceiling of 0 means unbounded.
panels.title: Compaction Memory Reserved vs Ceiling

panels.description: Segment compactions holding a reservation on this node right now, across every log it serves.
panels.title: Compactions Running

panels.description: Compactions this node declined, by gate. A refusal is not a failure -- the client tries another replica and the auditor retries next cycle. 'reservation' means compaction is at its own ceiling; 'memory_pressure' means the node is near its memory limit for reasons that may have nothing to do with compaction.
panels.title: Compaction Admission Rejects
R1 · Per-node headroom, fraction of its limit
panels.description: R1 fires when any node passes 70% CPU, 50% memory or 50% of its volume IOPS. Everything is drawn as a fraction of its own limit so one line reads for all three.

targets.expr: avg(sum by (instance) (rate(process_network_receive_bytes_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", job=~"$server_job"}[5m]) + rate(process_network_transmit_bytes_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", job=~"$server_job"}[5m]))) / $node_net_limit

panels.title: R2 · Cluster mean, all five must pass 50%
panels.description: R2 scales out only when every one of the five is over the line at once. Any single one crossing has other explanations -- CPU rises during compaction, network during read amplification.

panels.title: R6 · WAL disk free, and the 4h linear projection
panels.description: R6 fires when the projection goes below zero, which is earlier than any watermark alert. The rule also requires free > 0 so a disk that is already full reports through R5 instead of repeating here.

targets.expr: sum by (node_id, reason) (increase(woodpecker_server_compaction_admission_rejected_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[15m]))

panels.title: R7 · Compaction admissions declined, 15m
panels.description: reservation means the concurrency slot ran out; memory_pressure means the node crossed its memory watermark. The two have different fixes, so they are kept apart.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_file_flush_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[5m])))

panels.title: F4/F5 · Flush latency p99
panels.description: Milliseconds, matching the metric. Measured peak under load was 19.6 ms, so 100 ms leaves 5x and 500 ms is well into trouble.

panels.title: F6 · gRPC append handling p99
panels.description: Seconds here, unlike every woodpecker histogram next to it, which are milliseconds. Mixing the two is the easiest way to write a rule that never fires.

targets.expr: sum by (node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_object_storage_operations_total{SEL, status="error"}[5m])) / sum by (node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_object_storage_operations_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[5m]))

panels.title: F7/F8 · Object storage error ratio
panels.description: Writes survive object storage being down; compaction does not, so local disk starts filling. That is why 50% is a page and not a warning.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, operation) (rate(woodpecker_server_object_storage_operation_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[5m])))

panels.title: F9 · Object storage latency p99
panels.description: Milliseconds, so the rule threshold for 5s is 5000. Broken out by operation because a slow list and a slow put mean different things.

targets.expr: max(woodpecker_server_sync_scheduler_waiting{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}) / max(woodpecker_server_sync_scheduler_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"})

panels.title: S1 · Sync scheduler queue, multiples of capacity
panels.description: A full pool is normal under load -- raising the worker count made latency worse in testing. Only a queue far past capacity is a signal.

targets.expr: sum by (node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_logstore_operations_total{SEL, operation=~"add_entry.*", status="error"}[5m])) / sum by (node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_logstore_operations_total{SEL, operation=~"add_entry.*"}[5m]))

panels.title: S3 · AddEntry error ratio
panels.description: Both the single and batch operations, since they are separate label values. Disk-pressure rejections are by design and show up in R5, not here.

targets.expr: max(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_file_flush_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[5m])))) / quantile(0.5, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_file_flush_latency_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[5m]))))

panels.title: S4 · Slowest node vs the median, flush p99
panels.description: One slow node drags every quorum it belongs to, so the comparison that matters is against its peers rather than against an absolute latency.

targets.expr: max(sum by (selected_node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_quorum_node_selected_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[15m]))) / avg(sum by (selected_node_id) (rate(woodpecker_server_quorum_node_selected_total{namespace=~"$namespace", woodpecker_id=~"$woodpecker_id", log_ns=~"$log_ns", log_id=~"$log_id"}[15m])))

panels.title: S5 · Node selection skew, max over mean
panels.description: Counts how often each node was actually picked. The older quorum_selection_skew_total counts selection calls by mode and cannot localise skew to a node.

panels.title: S6 · Local reclaim against local growth, 1h
panels.description: Reclaim flat while local data grows means compaction is failing upstream. Reclaimed is a counter and takes increase(); stored bytes is a gauge and takes delta().

panels.title: Alerts — what the rules actually threshold
